title: Joel DeBartolo and Give me an A
summary: Buddy collapsed laughing when nervous bassist Joel answered his tuning gag.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I let guys go — I had to fire guys who basically, yeah guys he disagreed with also, but also there were guys that weren’t up to the level yet and had to go. I mean I’m not going to name names but there were guys that we had to do that. It was just part of the thing. And once he got somebody that he liked, Joel DeBartolo was really I think one of the ones that stayed for quite a bit and that was a kind of a story, I don’t know how much time you’ve got with that. But you know Joel had been working with my brother in

Rochester, with Gap Mangione’s band, and he had worked with Chuck Mangione and my brother Joe. And so I knew that he could play the gig. I hired him on the gig, he comes, and we were playing in St. Louis, Missouri in a big hotel, and Joel had never seen the book. Now Joel was kind of nervous, he was very nervous, and Joel had a stutter. He really had a problem stuttering. He ended up playing in the Tonight Show band with Johnny Carson for years. You know he was the bass player. So I got Joel on and Joel came on the bandstand and Buddy used to do this bit where he’d come out, and Dave Lama was the piano player and I think that was the time Dave was on, and Buddy would say, “Give me an A” and he’d yell down to the piano player. And the piano player would play an A and then Buddy would hit the snare drum and pretend he was tuning. Buddy comes on that night and he sees Joel back there and Joel is just shaking, and Buddy knows it’s like a deer in the headlights. So Buddy — and I’m just going oh god, I’m just saying oh please. And so Buddy turns, instead of going to him he turns around to Joel and he goes, “Give me an A.” And Joel went, “Aaaayyy” like that. Buddy fell on the floor, right off the stool, on the floor and was rolling around. He couldn’t play for twenty minutes. I mean he just could not stop laughing, Buddy. And Joel was in. Buddy just could not — and that was kind of an old bit that they used to do up in Rochester, all the Italians.
“Give me an A.” And you would just kind of trigger them.
That’s a classic story. I was so relieved after that, because Buddy loved him after that.
